name: highlight_part-77
title: Highlight a range
when: Use when one stretch of a sequence matters but the rest should stay fully visible for context, such as a range, a window, or the values that qualify.

verdict.notes: The box encloses 3–9 while 1 and 11 stay bright. At the end the box is still faintly visible, mid-fade. The box edges slightly clip neighbouring cells.

name: highlight_part-76
title: Highlight formula parts
when: Use when a sentence names one side or term of an equation and the rest of the formula should stay fully visible, with only a box moving between the parts.

verdict.notes: The full formula stays visible and the box switches from right to left. The hidden 'amount' box lingers as a faint ghost, a minor clutter flaw.

name: enclose_part-62
title: Brace a group
when: Use when one step or quantity applies to a whole group of items at once, so a brace over the group names that group as a single unit.

verdict.notes: A brace spans all ten cells with the label 'one update from all data'. Nothing overlaps or is cut off. The pattern carries over to other topics.

name: enclose_part-63
comment: Draw a rectangle bounding the points
title: Box a group
when: Use when several items should be treated as one group: a run of cells, a cluster, a subset the next sentence will talk about as a whole.

verdict.notes: Rounded box encloses cells 1–3 with label; the box slightly overlaps neighbor cell edges and index labels, but all stays readable.

name: cross_out-129
title: Cross out a claim
when: Use when a tempting implication, answer or step is shown and must be marked as wrong or ruled out while staying visible, such as a common misconception.

verdict.notes: A red X strikes out the claim while it stays visible, with a label below. The strokes cross the text but it remains readable. Sentence 1's pulse isn't visible in the still.

name: focus_isolate-43
title: Isolate one item
when: Use when several similar items are on stage and the next point is about just one of them: single it out so the rest recede and the voice can work on it alone.

verdict.notes: B stays bright while A and C recede. The others faded further mid-sentence, then partly returned by the end, but they still recede. Sentence 2 shows B isolated.

name: focus_isolate-44
title: Isolate one item
when: Use when several parallel items are on stage and the next point is about only one of them. The others fade to ghosts and stay faded, so the one item can be worked on without distraction.

verdict.notes: B and C fade to ghosts while A stays lit. They remain faded at the end, though slightly more visible than in frame 2. The hide lines plus focus are slightly redundant.

name: point_at-78
title: Pointer to a formula
when: Use when the learner should look at a formula, or one part of it, before it is unpacked. A pointer names the whole formula, then an enclosure moves the focus to one part.

verdict.notes: The arrow points at the whole formula, then the box moves focus to the numerator. The 'the update' label is still faintly visible after hide, a minor flaw.

name: point_at-83
title: Point at next guess
when: Use when a sentence names one spot (the next guess, a pivot, a pointer position) and that same marker will later move to a new spot.

verdict.notes: Red marker is labeled 'next guess' at 1.5, then slides to about 1.417 with its label following. The small 'N' label near the marker is a minor redundancy.

name: label_or_measure-48
title: Brace with new size
when: Use when a thing already on stage needs its size or count named, then restated in a more telling form, such as a total that turns out to be a square.

verdict.notes: The brace labelled 16 appears under the grid, then its label becomes 16 = 4². The 4×4 grid makes the square visible. The second brace replaced the first, which is fine.

name: reveal_one_by_one-55
title: Count one by one
when: Use when the order or the running count is the point: items arrive one after another and a tally keeps pace.

verdict.notes: Frames show only the end state, so one-by-one arrival isn't visible. The four numbered coins and the '4 coins' tally match the narration, and the layout is clean.

name: reveal_one_by_one-54
title: Reveal items one by one
when: Use when each item in a set gets its own matching thing and the count or order is the point, such as a vector per word, a result per input, or a tally building up.

verdict.notes: The frames show a vector paired with each word, labelled e1 to e3. The sentence-1 frame already shows all three, so the one-by-one build isn't visible, but the end state is correct.

name: write_formula-19
title: Write the equation
when: Use when a law or formula is stated for the first time and its symbols stand for things already on stage. The formula appears on the word that names it, and each symbol is coloured like its thing.

verdict.notes: The formula d = vt appears with v and t coloured like their bars. Layout is clean. The focus step is subtle, since nothing visibly dims, but the sentences are met.

name: write_formula-18
title: Write the equation
when: Use when a new law or formula should appear on screen as its own line, with its symbols then tied to the numbers they stand for.

verdict.notes: Formula appears as its own line, then m1 and m2 are tied to 16 and 1 by color and copy-send. Clean layout, no overlap.

name: transform_formula-69
title: Morph into simpler form
when: Use when one step of a derivation rewrites an expression into an equivalent, simpler one and a part carries through unchanged.

verdict.notes: The yellow 4! carries through while the right side collapses to 24. Frames show only the start and end states, not the morph itself, but both match the narration.

name: transform_formula-66
title: Exponentiate each part
when: Use when one step of a derivation applies the same function to every term of an expression already on screen, such as turning scores into e to the scores before normalizing.

verdict.notes: Frame 1 already shows the exponentiated result, so the original scores never appear in the frames. The morph is inferred. The end frame is clean, with e^x > 0 below.

name: substitute_values-146
title: Plug in a number
when: When a general expression or formula should be evaluated at one specific value, so the learner sees each symbol replaced by the number and then the arithmetic collapse to a result.

verdict.notes: Each x is replaced by 1, then the arithmetic collapses to 6. Frame 1 shows x three times, though the pulse isn't visible in the still.

name: compute_example-143
title: Worked numeric example
when: Use when a formula should be shown on one concrete number, substituted and simplified a step at a time until the result appears.

verdict.notes: Formula is substituted and simplified step by step to 4 bits, with a check. Frame 2 has a faint fading-parenthesis ghost, which is minor. The original formula with p is never seen.

name: compare_side_by_side-84
title: Compare side by side
when: Use when two cases computing the same kind of quantity should be contrasted, with both formulas and results staying visible, so the learner sees which is bigger.

verdict.notes: Both cases stay visible with formulas and results; the naive result is boxed as 'more bits'. Two rows are slightly misaligned, and the final-frame hs pulse is subtle.

name: compare_side_by_side-87
title: Compare side by side
when: Use when two cases of the same process or quantity must be contrasted, with both staying visible so the learner can see where they diverge.

verdict.notes: Both cases stay visible, stacked with identical structure and different outcomes. Stacked rather than literally side by side, but the contrast still reads clearly.

name: overlay-183
title: Match terms across equations
when: Use when two expressions have the same structure and the learner should see which term corresponds to which, such as an equation and its transformed version, or a model and its formula.

verdict.notes: Color-matched terms across the two stacked equations show the correspondence. The end frame shows no copies in flight, but the colors carry the mapping. The caption underlines and dictionary line are minor clutter.

name: swap_case-24
comment: Maybe do it for left variant, maybe not...
title: Swap in place
when: Use when one thing has several discrete variants or cases (functions, rules, versions) and you want to step through them one at a time in the same spot, so the eye compares them instead of hunting for a new place.

verdict.notes: The formula is swapped in place and ends as the cubic. The enclosure wraps the whole formula, not just the power, which slightly muddles 'only change'. Earlier variants aren't visible in the frames.

name: swap_case-25
title: Cycle through cases
when: Use when one slot or sentence has several alternative versions and you want to show them one after another, each replacing the last in place.

verdict.notes: The same array is replaced in place with formal, casual and code versions. Sentence 1's indicate pulse isn't visible in the frame. The final sentence's claim is only loosely shown.

name: move_object-32
title: Slide a thing away
when: Use when something should travel to a new place unchanged, while whatever is tied to it follows: a distance growing, a line stretching, a pushed object.

verdict.notes: The Sun ends up farther away and the line stretches with it. Only the end states are visible, so the motion itself is inferred. The Sun pulse in the last frame isn't clearly visible.

name: move_object-33
title: Park it aside
when: Use when a finished example must stay visible but get out of the way, because the next idea needs the space. The thing keeps its shape and glides to a new place.

verdict.notes: The example glides from center to the upper-left and shrinks slightly, keeping its shape and label. It stays visible and clear, and the pattern is generic.

name: sweep_scan-162
title: Sweep line over waveform
when: Use when a tutor wants to examine a function, signal or sequence one moment at a time: a marker travels along the axis and reads off the value where it lands.

verdict.notes: Both frames show the line and dot at x=10, so the sweep itself isn't visible. The 'time' label crowds the '10' tick. The indicate pulse isn't visible at the end.

name: vary_parameter-12
comment: Move s around, end at i
title: Slide a value, watch followers
when: Use when one quantity should be dragged through several values (a point, a parameter) while a readout and the picture that depend on it update live.

verdict.notes: The point slides from -1 to 0, then up to i. The trail and the live formula update with it. The plane's x-axis shows -5..5 rather than the declared [-2,2], which is minor.

name: vary_parameter-15
comment: Show four points going to a square
title: Slide four points apart
when: Use when a shape or configuration depends on one setting and you want to show it forming as that setting changes, such as points reaching a special arrangement or a family of cases settling into one.

verdict.notes: Points spread from bunched to the square as s changes. Frame 1's four labels crowd one dot but don't overlap. Square appears at the end.

name: grow_shrink-96
title: Shrink one bar
when: Use when comparing two quantities and one should visibly drop to a fraction of the other, e.g. a cost cut to 60% or a second option that turns out smaller.

verdict.notes: Both bars start at 10, the second shrinks to 6 and stays clearly shorter. The indicate pulse isn't visible in the final frame, but the shorter bar is.

name: transform_space-104
title: Shear back into square
when: Use when a shape or the whole plane is deformed by a matrix, and the point is that undoing the shear returns the original. Examples are a shear, a change of basis, or showing two shapes are the same up to a linear map.

verdict.notes: Grid and parallelogram shear back into a square together. Frames are clean and readable, and each sentence matches what is on stage. The pattern generalizes to other linear maps.

name: transform_space-105
title: Transform a vector
when: Use when a tutor wants to show what a matrix or mapping does: the input arrow stays, a copy carries to its image while the whole plane deforms.

verdict.notes: The grid shears, the input arrow stays, and the copy lands at (3,1). The grid is a bit dense, but the labels are clear.

name: decompose_split-134
title: Split into parts
when: Use when a tutor wants to show what a whole is made of: break one thing into its pieces and keep the total visible.

verdict.notes: One grey block splits into three colored, labeled parts, and the 'the same 12' total label stays visible. The parts are proportional to 6, 4 and 2, so the move reads clearly.

name: combine_gather-157
comment: Show the sum of the two vectors
title: Draw the sum arrow
when: Use when two quantities that add (vectors, phasors, forces, waves) should be shown combining into one result: draw the sum as its own arrow from the origin, in its own colour.

verdict.notes: Green sum arrow appears from the origin in its own colour. The equation is colour-matched and nothing overlaps. The axes rescale at the end, which is a minor flaw.

name: connect_map-116
title: Arrow from thing to code
when: Use when something is translated into another form, such as a phrase into bits, a word into a number, or an input into its representation. Show the source, then draw the arrow to its image.

verdict.notes: Source box, arrow labelled 'encode', and output box are clear. The pulse on the code in sentence 3 isn't visible in the end frame, but the content is on stage.

name: connect_map-115
comment: Built in the order they'll actually be revealed (increasing first, then decreasing), so any bar shared between the two gets its decreasing dot correctly nested inside the increasing one.
title: Reveal link families in turn
when: Use when two kinds of relation share some of the same things and you want each family drawn as its own batch, in order, so the viewer sees where they overlap.

verdict.notes: Green batch appears first, then orange batch, sharing nodes 3 and 4. The frame at sentence 2 is mid-layout, but the end frame is clean. Orange arrowheads at node 2 sit close together.

name: show_structure-120
title: Show a ladder of levels
when: Use when a scale of reference levels, such as bits, tiers or thresholds, should appear all at once as one organised structure that later items are measured against.

verdict.notes: The table appears all at once as a ladder of levels. The frames are clean. The pulse in sentence 2 is subtle, but the doubling is visible in the table.

name: show_structure-125
title: Show the ring
when: Use when items belong in a cycle or loop (seasons, notes, clock hours) and the whole arrangement should appear at once, so the viewer sees the shape before any single item.

verdict.notes: Ring and four labelled season dots are fully visible by sentence 1. Sentence 2's spring pulse isn't visibly distinct, but both seasons are on stage.

name: plot_graph-151
title: Extend the graph
when: Use when a function is known only on a stretch and the point is that the same rule keeps going beyond it: analytic continuation, extrapolation, or a formula outside its first domain.

verdict.notes: The orange extension continues the blue curve on both sides. A stray auto-label 'Right' appears, and no indicate pulse is visible in the end frame.

name: show_distribution-179
title: Bars for probabilities
when: Use when a tutor wants to show a distribution as bars, one per outcome, each as tall as its probability, building up one at a time.

verdict.notes: Bars appear in order with heights proportional to probability. The 0.125 value displays as 0.12, a minor rounding quirk. The final b4 pulse isn't visible in a still frame.

name: run_process-1
title: Predict the next word
when: Use when introducing a model that reads an input and outputs a single guess, such as next-word prediction, a classifier's label, or a function's output.

verdict.notes: Input flows through the model to a single output word. Layout is clean and the text is readable. The pattern generalizes to classifiers and functions.

name: run_process-2
title: Let time pass
when: Use when a process should simply play out on its own clock, such as an infection, a decay or a simulation, and the learner watches what changes while a visible counter ticks.

verdict.notes: The counter ticks from day 0 to day 5 while the virus bar drains to 0 and is relabelled 'recovered'. Frame 2 shows 0.21 mid-settle, which is minor.

name: geometric_construction-109
comment: Draw a set of local axes labeled dx and dy
title: Local axes at a point
when: Use when you want to measure a small change at one spot on a curve, such as a derivative, a linearisation or a tangent, and need a fresh pair of axes (dx across, df up) centred on that spot.

verdict.notes: Small grey dx/df axes sit centred on P and the zoom fills the view with them. The labels are a bit small, but nothing overlaps.

name: geometric_construction-111
title: Drop lines to axes
when: Use when a point's coordinates, or a pair of numbers, need to be read off a plane. Drop one auxiliary line to each axis so each number has a visible source.

verdict.notes: Both drop lines are clearly drawn. The x=3, P and y=2 labels crowd near the point without overlapping. The axis range shown (-2 to 8) differs from the schema's 0–6.

name: show_field-169
title: Flash in direction
when: Use when a single direction (a difference vector, a force, a drift) should be felt as a whole field. Show the arrow once, then fill the space with flow lines that all stream along it.

verdict.notes: The arrow appears first, then flow lines fill the stage along the same direction. Lines pass behind the arrow and label slightly, but nothing is obscured.

name: two_views-172
title: Picture and numbers
when: Use when one thing has two representations that should stay tied together, such as an image and its pixel values, a curve and its formula, or arrows and a matrix.

verdict.notes: The 'picture' is drawn as numbered cells like the numbers view, so the two views look identical. The focus on nums at the end doesn't visibly dim the picture.

name: zoom_in-9
title: Zoom in on detail
when: Use when one small part of a bigger picture needs a closer look, such as a point on a curve, a cell, or a region. Zoom in on the word that names it, then reset to restore the context.

verdict.notes: Camera zooms on P, the curve looks straight, then it resets to the full view. The curve's end touches the f(x) label slightly, which is minor.

name: zoom_out_reset-37
title: Zoom out to restore
when: Use after zooming into a detail, to hand the whole picture back and show how the detail fits in the context.

verdict.notes: Frame 1 is zoomed in on P and the curve looks straight. The end frame restores the full axes and curve with P marked. Nothing overlaps or is cut off.

name: zoom_out_reset-38
title: Zoom back out
when: Use after zooming into a detail, to hand the whole picture back and tie the detail to the bigger structure.

verdict.notes: Zoomed view shows a near-straight line at P; the reset shows the full curve bending. The f label sits close to the top edge but stays readable.

name: fade_remove-93
title: Dim the claim aside
when: Use when a rule or claim has done its job and you want to set it aside, without deleting it, so a counterexample or new case gets the viewer's full attention.

verdict.notes: The claim card dims but stays visible while the root jumps to a new spot. The trail isn't visible, but each sentence's action shows on stage.

name: fade_remove-95
title: Remove one thing
when: Use when a tutor needs to take one item out of a set, such as a removed square, a dropped case or an eliminated option, while leaving it visible as a faint ghost.

verdict.notes: S6 fades to a faint ghost while S1–S5 stay bright. The layout is clean with no overlaps, and each sentence matches its frame.
